title: Aft Lower Shell Skin Panel — External Patch Repair Below the Cargo Floor Line
abstract: Permanent external patch repair for pitting and thinning of the lower shell skin panel below the cargo floor line in the aft fuselage, applied from outside with the panel left in place.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the pressure and shear capability of the lower shell skin panel in the aft fuselage after external pitting or thinning has been removed, without disturbing the internal structure.
sections.damage_assessment: Map the affected area from outside with an ultrasonic thickness scan on a 20 mm grid, extending at least 150 mm beyond the visible edge of the damage. Damage confined to a single skin bay, not crossing a stringer or a frame line, and leaving at least 80 per cent of nominal thickness after clean-up, is inside this repair. Damage that crosses a stringer, that lies within 50 mm of an existing patch, or that leaves less than 80 per cent of nominal thickness is outside it. Where the thinning is accompanied by delaminated paint over a wider area, treat the whole discoloured region as suspect and scan it before deciding the patch size. Photograph the mapped area with a scale before any material is removed.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the damaged material by rotary abrasion to a smooth dish, keeping the length to depth ratio above thirty to one, and blend the edges. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the cleaned area. Cut the external patch from the doubler kit D5331120951225 to the layout of repair drawing RD-53-31-12-004 and drill the fastener pattern using the patch as a template. Where the patch spans a lug position, add the local packer from the sub-assembly GI662328-74 shown on sheet 2. Deburr and apply the surface protection of the standard practice to all new surfaces. Install the patch wet with sealant, using the fastener set from the kit and the pitch and edge distance on the drawing. Where the lug kit HOD868414-75 or the stiffener kit CIN549365-19 lies under the patch footprint, do not fasten through it; the drawing shows the exclusion zone. Fit silicone edging grommets AES252500-3C at any systems penetration inside the patch boundary. Restore the external finish to aerodynamic smoothness class B.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 18 000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. Do a repeat eddy current inspection of the patch perimeter and of the blended dish every 4 500 flight cycles. Do a detailed visual inspection of the patch edge sealant at every zonal inspection of the area; a lifted edge admits water and invalidates the repair. Any new indication inside the patch boundary requires a fresh engineering assessment. Report the repair to Aeralis so that it is recorded against the aircraft.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Damage confined to one skin bay, not crossing a stringer or frame line, not closer than 50 mm to an existing patch, and leaving at least 80 per cent of nominal thickness after clean-up.

type_data.fastener_pattern: Three rows, 96 fasteners total, 20 mm pitch and 14 mm edge distance, staggered, with the exclusion zone on sheet 2 left unfastened

title: Aft Lower Shell Skin Panel — External Patch Repair Below the Cargo Floor Line

issue.reason: The certification position on an external patch combined with an internal frame foot renewal in the same bay is stated, together with what happens to the patch perimeter inspection.

Where the internal frame foot in the same bay has been renewed, or is planned for renewal, the patch is outside this repair until the combined case has been assessed; see the inspection requirements below. Combined case with the internal frame foot renewal: an external patch on the lower shell and a renewed frame foot on the inside of the same bay form a stack that neither substantiation covers on its own, because the patch was sized against the original internal stiffness and the renewal was sized against an unpatched skin. Structures certification has ruled that the combination is acceptable provided the patch boundary stays at least 60 mm clear of the renewed foot flange, and that the patch perimeter inspection continues unchanged at its own interval after the renewal, under the repair record and not under the modification. Where the 60 mm cannot be held, the patch is removed and the skin bay assessed as a new case before the renewal proceeds.
